segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good afternoon everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, with some of you about to go out on field work it's timely that in this afternoon's session I'll be sharing some ideas about the reasons why groups of whales and dolphins sometimes swim ashore from the sea right onto the beach and, most often, die in what are known as 'mass standings'.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Unfortunately, this type of event is a frequent occurrence in some of the locations that you'll be travelling to, where sometimes the tide goes out suddenly , confusing the animals.However, there are many other theories about the causes of mass strandings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The first is that the behaviour is linked to parasites.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's often found that stranded animals were infested with large numbers of parasites.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For instance, a type of worm is commonly found in the ears of dead whales.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Since marine animals rely heavily on their hearing to navigate, this type of infestation has the potential to be very harmful .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Another theory is related to toxins, or poisons.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These have also been found to contribute to the death of many marine animals.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Many toxins, as I'm sure vou're aware, originate from plants, or animals .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The whale ingests these toxins in its normal feeding behaviour but whether these poisons directly or indirectly lead to stranding and death, seems to depend upon the toxin involved.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In 1988, for example, fourteen humpback whales examined after stranding along the beaches of Cape Cod were found to have been poisoned after eating tuna that contained saxitoxin, the same toxin that can be fatal in humans.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Alternatively, it has also been suggested that some animals strand accidentally by following their prey ashore in the confusion of the chase.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In 1995 David Thurston monitored pilot whales that beached after following squid ashore.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, this idea does not seem to hold true for the majority of mass strandings because examination of the animals' stomach contents reveal that most had not been feeding as thev stranded .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are also some new theories which link strandings to humans.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A growing concern is that loud noises in the ocean cause strandings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Noises such as those caused bv military exercises are of particular concern and have been pinpointed as the cause of some strandings of late .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One of these, a mass stranding of whales in 2000 in the Bahamas coincided closely with experiments using a new submarine detection system.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There were several factors that made this stranding stand out as different from previous strandings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This led researchers to look for a new cause.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For one, all the stranded animals were healthy .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In addition, the animals were spread out along 38 kilometres of coast , whereas it's more common for the animals to be found in a group when mass strandings occur.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A final theory is related to group behaviour, and suggests that sea mammals cannot distinguish between sick and healthy leaders and will follow sick leaders, even to an inevitable death.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is a particularly interesting theory since the whales that are thought to be most social - the toothed whales - are the group that strand the most frequently .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The theory is also supported by evidence from a dolphin stranding in 1994.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Examination of the dead animals revealed that apart from the leader, all the others had been healthy at the time of their death.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Without one consistent theory however it is very hard for us to do anything about this phenomenon except to assist animals where and when we can.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Stranding networks have been established around the world to aid in rescuing animals and collecting samples from those that could not be heloed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I recommend John Connor's Marine Mammals Ashore as an excellent starting point if you're interested in finding out more about these networks , or establishing one yourself.
